claims.text: A controlled low-energy laser beam with an optimized scanning pattern will reduce residual thermal stresses in additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
The proposed deposition strategy will improve the mechanical properties of additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi miniature components.
The proposed intervention will refine the grains.
The proposed intervention will produce a homogeneous microstructure.
Optimized heat input and scanning will reduce thermal gradients.
Optimized heat input and scanning will reduce stress accumulation.
Yield strength will increase by 20–30% relative to components made under conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions.
Ductility will increase by 10–20% relative to components made under conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing conditions.
The applicable laser-power window is 100–200 W.
The applicable scanning-speed window is 500–1000 mm/s.
The applicable layer-thickness window is 20–50 μm.
The hypothesis applies to miniature components with complex geometries and feature sizes below 1 mm.
The magnitude of the mechanical-property improvement depends on the scanning pattern and process parameters.

contradictions.description: The prediction specifies 20–30% and 10–20% improvements, but the falsification rule tests only whether improvements are statistically significant rather than whether those quantitative ranges are achieved.
The rule describes an outcome as 'not significantly higher' while assigning p < 0.05, which ordinarily denotes statistical significance.
